parsed.explanation: The state/province is genuinely protective — constitutional equality clause, public-accommodation and hate-crime coverage, marker changes without surgery, X designations, care-coverage mandates, 2023 correctional protections, and a July 2026 low-risk rating. But the traveller meets the combined regime: the parent's entry cable directs refusal on any document discrepancy or doubt about sex, permits fraud/lifetime-ineligibility referral, bars X markers, subjects travellers to outing-prone screening, restricts federally funded single-sex facilities, and documents abusive immigration custody with beatings and sexual abuse. State law does not cancel federal entry, screening or custody. Working state courts and protections mitigate street, service and care exposure but not the federal layer.

entry_documents.exposure: Parent framework: Feb 2025 cable directs officers to refuse cases where documents cast doubt on sex, and to weigh fraud findings carrying possible permanent ineligibility; X markers barred; document discrepancies reported to cause confiscation. Universal-exposure for outed or mismatched travellers. Documented.
entry_documents.protection: State issues corrected-gender birth certificates on affidavits and X state IDs; existing foreign X passports remain valid until expiry; litigation pending and some measures enjoined. Documented but national in scope and does not govern entry decisions.
entry_documents.interaction: State-level document leniency cannot cure a federal visa or border refusal; a state-issued X ID may itself trigger the cable's discrepancy-refusal rule at entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented abuse in federal immigration custody: transgender men subjected to forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. Federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026; custody figures no longer reported. State custody has a 2023 protection law but assessment finds it short in operation.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2023 state correctional protection statute; state hate-crime penalties; functioning courts. State remedies do not reach federal immigration custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A traveller denied entry or held on a discrepancy moves from state protection into federal custody where documented abuse occurs; the state cannot intervene.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; 19 state/provinces restrict facilities, 4 criminalise in some circumstances, one documented arrest. Whether this state restricts facilities is not documented; public-accommodation law cuts the other way.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State anti-discrimination law since 2011 covering public accommodation; constitution-level equality protection since 2022; hate-crime hotline. Documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facilities rules still bind nationally funded buildings within the state; the state's facility status is an open question, not a documented protection.

care_services.exposure: Federal level: June 2025 ruling upholding youth-care bans, January 2025 orders framing care as 'mutilation', proposed federal insurance exclusions for under-18s — relevant to a travelling minor. Assessment finds state healthcare equity shortfalls, qualitatively stated.
care_services.protection: State mandates insurer and public-programme coverage of medically necessary gender-affirming treatment (Jan 2024) and bans insurance discrimination; conversion therapy on minors banned. Documented and operative.
care_services.interaction: An adult visitor's care access rests on state law plus own insurance; a minor's care is contested between protective state law and hostile federal orders and rulings.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' ideologies for prioritised identification; December 2025 reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology' language; orders direct investigating 'gender ideology' in schools. Rhetorical and institutional hostility, not documented enforcement against visitors. Documented as framing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Rewards explicitly are not keyed to gender views; state non-discrimination, hate-crime law and 2019 gay-panic repeal. Documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal hostility sets climate and may embolden individual officers; state equality law constrains state, not federal, actors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal orders criminalise facilitation of a trans minor's social transition, frame youth care as mutilation, and back a June 2025 ruling upholding care bans; school sports body now requires birth-sex competition; state 2026 ballot initiative on sports failed. A visibly trans minor or parent risks scrutiny.
minors_guardians.protection: State anti-bullying law listing gender identity (2015), care-coverage mandate, conversion-therapy ban; state schools' policies still protective in part. Documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family entering federally screened with a mismatched or questioned document faces the entry-refusal rule while state schools and clinics remain protective.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No incident of anti-trans violence in this state with date and outcome appears in the dossier; no state-level pattern can be described. 23 state/provinces cover gender identity in bias statutes and only 22 plus capital outlaw discrimination — but this state is among the protective ones.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime statute covering gender identity since 2013, reporting hotline since Jan 2025, gay-panic defence repealed, robust non-discrimination regime; July 2026 assessment rates the state low-risk. Documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to a street incident would fall under functioning state institutions; federal screening remains the more likely adverse encounter.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal measures are partly enjoined but unresolved, so exposure varies by travel date; the state's facility-map entry, airport document handling, and the size of the state's healthcare and incarceration shortfalls are not documented. Litigation outcomes uncertain.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation against the passport policy, an active legal-aid FAQ, constitutional equality clause, functioning state courts, and a national risk assessment placing the state one tier below most protective. Documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working state courts mitigate state-level friction but cannot reverse a federal refusal, fraud finding or federal custody condition.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this. Vellandra's register excludes all trans visitors with internal appeals and no real remedy; here refusal is discretionary under a cable, litigation is live, courts function, and the state affirmatively protects. Documented custody abuse keeps this from higher, but the entry mechanism is less absolute and universal than a register.

Lower than this. Kestrel Isles' secondary screening yields administrative refusal and return transport with slow remedies. Here the cable directs refusal on discrepancy, opens a possible permanent fraud ineligibility, and federal immigration custody carries documented beatings and sexual abuse — materially more severe than administrative turnaround.

Higher than this. Meridia trains border officers, recognises trans passports, detains only briefly, and offers counsel and compensation through a working tribunal. This dossier documents the opposite federal posture — mismatch-triggered refusal, X-marker ban, abusive custody — so it cannot sit near the 0.75 tier despite strong state protections.

parsed.synthesis: Two regimes operate on one traveller. The state/province supplies genuine, documented protections: constitutional equality, public-accommodation and hate-crime coverage, surgery-free marker changes with X designations, care-coverage mandates, and functioning courts — enough for a July 2026 low-risk rating. The parent framework supplies the exposures a visitor actually cannot avoid: an entry cable that refuses on document discrepancy and contemplates permanent fraud findings, X-marker prohibition, outing-prone screening, federally funded facility restrictions, hostile federal rhetoric and care policy, and immigration custody with documented beatings and sexual abuse. State law does not reach border desks or federal custody, so the protective layer cannot cancel the federal one. The result is elevated risk concentrated at entry, screening and any detention, with comparatively low everyday risk in the state itself; a travelling minor sits in contested space between protective state care law and hostile federal orders.
